title: Agent Teams, Evals and Observability
summary: Coordinate specialized agents without creating opaque, untestable automation.
sections: 1. Specialization beats vague autonomy

A useful agent has a narrow role, source set, tool permissions, output schema and stop conditions. “Do everything” agents are difficult to evaluate and dangerous to authorize. A team can divide profile interpretation, research, architecture, mission design, assessment and QA while sharing a common learner brief.
2. Independent criticism

Do not let the same agent that created an output be its only reviewer. Use a separate QA or red-team role to challenge unsupported assumptions, unsafe actions, weak evidence and missing edge cases. The critic should have permission to reject and request revision.
3. Evals

Create known test cases with expected properties. Include normal cases, adversarial prompts, missing data, conflicting sources, permission boundaries and tempting hallucination opportunities. Measure whether the system catches them consistently before production.
4. Observability

Log inputs, outputs, tool calls, errors, retries, latency, model/version, user corrections and final acceptance. Monitor false positives, false negatives and exception frequency. Observability lets you improve the system based on evidence rather than anecdotes.

title: Nexus: AI Transformation for Real Businesses
summary: Translate AI capability into measurable SMB outcomes through diagnosis, prioritization, implementation, governance and proof.
objectives: Build an evidence chain for results
sections: 1. Diagnose before prescribing

Begin with current state: workflow, people, systems, volumes, time, errors, bottlenecks, handoffs and baseline metrics. Define desired state and gap. Only then identify AI opportunities. The purpose is not to sell an agent; it is to improve a business outcome.
2. Prioritize opportunities

Score each opportunity on value, feasibility, data readiness, integration complexity, adoption burden, risk and reversibility. Fast wins are repetitive, high-volume, low-risk, measurable and currently painful. Avoid starting with the most glamorous automation.
3. Pilot and govern

Build the smallest safe pilot that can validate the thesis. Preserve human control over payments, legal commitments, deletion, permissions, hiring/firing and other material consequences. Define success metrics, exception paths, rollback and ownership before launch.
4. Prove value honestly

Record baseline source, post-launch source, formula, assumptions, third-party costs, adoption context and confounders. Use measured or estimated language when causation is uncertain. Testimonials and case studies require explicit authorization.

title: Statecraft: Human Development in an AI-Rich World
summary: Use AI to support human agency, reflection and experimentation without turning self-development into hidden profiling.
objectives: Apply Current State → Gap → Desired State
sections: 1. State before strategy

Improvement begins with a clear current state, a desired state, and the gap between them. Describe observable conditions rather than vague identity labels. The desired state should reflect what the person actually wants, not what the system infers they should want.
2. AI as reflection partner

AI can summarize patterns, generate questions, propose experiments and compare outcomes. It should not claim certainty about a person’s psychology or destiny. Good personalization is explicit: the user can see, correct, export or delete the information being used.
3. Experiments over proclamations

Convert advice into small experiments with a hypothesis, action, duration, measurement and reflection. This keeps the system reality-based. A failed experiment generates information instead of becoming a moral judgment.
4. Human premium

As generated content becomes abundant, lived experience, authenticity, relationships, embodied practice, judgment and meaning become differentiators. Statecraft can teach people how to use AI without outsourcing the human work of choosing values and taking responsibility.

applications.Nexus: Use explicit client goals rather than hidden profiling.
applications.Career: Run role/skill experiments instead of relying on identity stories.
applications.Trading: Separate emotional reflection from deterministic rule tracking.
